name: Erase and Extend (Hard Version)
description: This is the hard version of the problem. The only difference is the constraints on $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$. You can make hacks only if all versions of the problem are solved. You have a string $$$s$$$, and you can do two types of operations on it: Delete the last character of the string. Duplicate the string: $$$s:=s+s$$$, where $$$+$$$ denotes concatenation. You can use each operation any number of times (possibly none). Your task is to find the lexicographically smallest string of length exactly $$$k$$$ that can be obtained by doing these operations on string $$$s$$$. A string $$$a$$$ is lexicographically smaller than a string $$$b$$$ if and only if one of the following holds: $$$a$$$ is a prefix of $$$b$$$, but $$$a\ne b$$$; In the first position where $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ differ, the string $$$a$$$ has a letter that appears earlier in the alphabet than the corresponding letter in $$$b$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \leq n, k \leq 5\cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the original string $$$s$$$ and the length of the desired string. The second line contains the string $$$s$$$, consisting of $$$n$$$ lowercase English letters.
output_specification: Print the lexicographically smallest string of length $$$k$$$ that can be obtained by doing the operations on string $$$s$$$.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
